rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline contains enough predictive signal to justify more complex multiprofile or multimodal designs. This experiment tests the simplest RNA representation: single-profile PCA with no aggregation or fusion, providing a clean reference point for later comparisons of profile aggregation, advanced RNA encoders, image-only baselines, and fusion. It is the best first use of budget because it is low-cost, avoids confounding multiple design choices, and establishes the baseline needed to interpret all subsequent experiments.

The only completed result is RNA-only single-profile PCA (accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), leaving uncertainty about whether multiple profiles improve performance. config_002 keeps the model setting and RNA encoder fixed while adding multiprofile with simple avgpool, directly testing the profile/aggregation effect relative to the baseline. This is the best next experiment because it is a controlled, low-risk extension that avoids simultaneously introducing image modality, a new RNA encoder, or fusion, and it will clarify whether multiprofile aggregation is worth further exploration.

The main evidence is that RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool improved substantially over singleprofile PCA, but this change also introduced aggregation, so the source of improvement is not fully isolated. config_003 tests transformer aggregation while keeping the same RNA encoder and multiprofile setting, clarifying whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool. This is a one-factor extension of the most promising current result, making it an efficient next experiment under the limited budget.

RNA-only PCA results show multiprofile avgpool is clearly the best RNA setting (0.591 accuracy vs 0.485 singleprofile and 0.519 transformer), but there is no evidence yet for the image modality. config_011 tests image-only ResNet50 under the same multiprofile avgpool setting, isolating the image representation without introducing fusion. This establishes whether image can be competitive with the RNA baseline and whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing, making it a high-value, low-confound use of the next budgeted experiment.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), clearly better than singleprofile PCA and multiprofile transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is much weaker. The main remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA under the same already-promising profile and aggregation settings. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, isolating the representation effect while exploiting the best RNA-only direction. This is more informative than moving to multimodal fusion, which would change multiple factors at once and could confound whether any gain comes from the RNA encoder, image data, or fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile avgpool is the strongest direction, with scvi_n200 improving over PCA by about 6 points in accuracy and 5.5 points in F1, while image-only performance is weak. The main remaining uncertainty is whether scvi_n200 is the best RNA representation or whether scgpt can match or exceed it. config_008 keeps profile setting and aggregation fixed at the current best settings and changes only the RNA encoder, cleanly isolating the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it can either improve the current best RNA baseline or confirm that scvi_n200 is the preferred encoder before investing in more complex multimodal or fusion settings.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool (0.6501 accuracy, 0.6275 F1), and PCA multiprofile showed avgpool outperforming transformer (0.5907 vs 0.5191). This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation can improve or match the best scvi representation while changing only aggregation. It is a focused, one-factor extension that clarifies whether aggregation matters for the strongest unimodal baseline before spending budget on multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence is for RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile models (config_006: 0.6530 accuracy, 0.6283 F1; config_005: 0.6501 accuracy, 0.6275 F1), and multiprofile already helped for PCA (config_002 vs config_001). However, it is unclear whether the best RNA encoder, scvi_n200, also depends on multiprofile aggregation or can perform well with a simpler single-profile setup. config_004 tests scvi_n200 singleprofile, isolating the profile-setting effect while keeping the encoder fixed and avoiding simultaneous changes to image or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about a core design choice, may reveal a simpler strong baseline, and is more informative than jumping directly to multimodal configurations.

RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile models are currently strongest, while the only image-only test (resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool) was weak. It is unclear whether image features can be useful at all or whether resnet50 is simply a poor image representation. config_014 tests imagenet_vit_l under the same image-only multiprofile avgpool setting as config_011, isolating the effect of image encoder choice. This is the best next step because it reduces uncertainty about whether the image modality is worth combining before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion configurations.

RNA-only evidence is strongest for multiprofile scvi_n200, with avgpool reaching 0.6501 accuracy and transformer 0.6530, while image-only models are weak around 0.33. The main remaining uncertainty is whether adding image information to the strong scvi RNA representation improves performance. config_036 tests this by extending the tested scvi_n200 multiprofile avgpool RNA baseline with imagenet_vit_l image features using the same avgpool aggregation and a simple concat fusion. This is the best next experiment because it directly probes the highest-value untested choice—multimodal fusion—while minimizing confounds from untested transformer image aggregation or weighted fusion.
